rules_text:
Rules summary Contents 1 Objective 2 Game Structure 2.1 1. Activation 2.2 2. Engagement 3 Day and Night 4 The Final Battle Objective To win, you must travel through the forest, reach Grandma’s Cabin, and defeat the Big Bad Wolf. You lose the game if your Health drops to 0. Game Structure Each round consists of two main parts: Activation and Engagement. 1. Activation This phase handles movement and preparation: Exploration (Optional): Choose up to 3 dice and roll them one by one. Miss: Add a Nighttime forest card to the end of your path. Hit: Add a Daytime forest card to the path. Crit: Add a Daytime card + gain 1 Gold. Visit Merchant: Spend Gold to buy or upgrade an item or to recover exhausted or banished dice. Travel: Move your hero along the lines to the next node. Enemy/Wolf Nodes: Activate cards from the scouting line to face them. Fable Nodes: Draw a card and resolve its unique story effect. Campfire Nodes: Permanently increase one of your stats (Health, Strategy, or Recovery). Bribery: You may pay Gold to discard non-boss enemies and avoid fighting them. 2. Engagement If enemies remain in the active area, combat begins: Strategy Phase: Commit and roll dice to defeat enemies. You can repeat this process a number of times equal to your Strategy stat. Resolve Phase: Take damage from remaining enemies, exhaust used dice, and recover dice based on your Recovery stat. Day and Night Forest cards feature a green Daytime side (easier) and a purple Nighttime side (more dangerous). Effects or failed exploration rolls may flip cards or force you to add difficult Nighttime cards to your path. The Final Battle When the forest deck is empty and you reach the Cabin, the Big Bad Wolf emerges. Any remaining Wolf Pack cards turn into Power-Ups that strengthen the boss. The endgame continues until the Wolf is defeated or your hero perishes.

[Rating: 2/10] The rules for this game are a disaster. They are split across two books, requiring to read an abstract set of base rules, then modify them in the specific book. Worse still, they are contradictory. Both the printed books and the official videos state a rule in the base version and then state something different in the specific book while saying "as in the base rules".

[Rating: 3/10] I've cooled significantly on this game. Even with easiest difficulty settings, 2-3 bad rolls can mean the game is over at any point of playing

[Rating: 3/10] Nothing seems well thought-out or balanced. The end boss is incredibly swingy, which makes the entire run feel pointless. Some items are much worse than others and don't feel very interesting. Some enemy powers feel too punishing, especially when there can be 4-5 enemies at once.

[Rating: 3/10] I love the artwork and the theme. Components are great. But that's about it. There is not much of a game here. This version of 20 Strong is even more random than Solar Sentinels.

[Rating: 3.5/10] Yeah, this system isn't for me. There are many twists and changes in this version, when compared with the base game - you even move around a map (in a similar vein of that of Slay the Spire).   Is still hard, luck-based and frustrating as hell. But it is an improvement over the base game, with more options on how to proceed towards the final battle.

[Rating: 4/10] Cull pile. The game play loop of committing and recovering dice just isn't fun for me.

[Rating: 5/10] The slay the spire inspired gameplay is great. Having said that, I'm not sure how you compete against three enemies with HP 6, 6, and 3 in your third battle. Feels more random punishing than solar sentinels, which I didn't care for either.

[Rating: 5/10] Backed GameFound in July of 2024, delivered Sept 2025.  I kind of like the "Slay the Spire" inspired game layout, but overall I find it fiddly, overly complicated and punishing in a way that's not fun.
